- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots downward in next 3–5 days; cap forecast decline to 5–10% below peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast slope slightly to match sentiment momentum.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 1–2% upward bias in middle-to-late forecast period.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth 3–5 day forecast transitions to avoid erratic swings.
- Forecast often lags sentiment shifts by 1–2 days; adjust model to anticipate sentiment change 1 day ahead, especially if sentiment is trending.
